1	{"body":"## Description\n\nFixes custom reports still counting a subcategory after it's unchecked in the category list (#100). Before this change, unchecking a subcategory didn't change the report: its amount stayed in the parent category's total. If the parent was unchecked and a subcategory was left checked, the subcategory's amount showed up under the parent's name.\n\n- **`subcategories.ts`:**\n  - Custom reports now apply the category checkbox filter exactly as written. Before, any parent in the filter had all of its subcategories added back, so unchecked ones were still fetched.\n  - A subcategory only rolls into its parent's row when both are checked. One checked without its parent is shown as its own row.\n- **`custom-spreadsheet.ts` / `grouped-spreadsheet.ts`:** both use the new filter handling and the narrowed roll-up. This covers every graph type (Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Table), Budgeted mode and dashboard widgets.\n- **`showActivity.ts`:** clicking a parent's bar or row keeps the report's category filter as written, so the transaction list leaves out unchecked subcategories and matches the row.\n- **`CustomReport.tsx`:** the check for filters too complex for the checkboxes now comes from a shared helper, so the checkboxes and the report read the filter the same way.\n\nReport totals now stay correct whichever parents and subcategories are checked.\n\n## Design Decisions\n\n- **Keep subcategories rolled into the parent's bar, and only fix which ones are included.** The issue also asks to see how much each subcategory contributes. This PR doesn't change the graphs, so it stays small and fixes the incorrect totals first. Two alternatives were considered:\n  1. **Show each subcategory as its own bar.**\n     - Pros: fits every graph type.\n     - Cons: needs a new saved report option (database migration, report types, sidebar toggle, dashboard widgets), plus click-through changes in five graph components. Without a toggle it would change how every existing report looks.\n     - Status: left as a follow-up.\n  2. **Split each parent's bar into coloured segments, one per subcategory.**\n     - Pros: looks good for Bar, and possibly Donut.\n     - Cons: doesn't carry over to Stacked Bar (which already stacks categories over time), Line or Area, so behaviour would be inconsistent across graph types. Also needs per-segment data, colours, tooltips, legend and click handling, and new visual regression snapshots. It wouldn't fix the totals on its own either; this PR's filter change is still needed underneath.\n- **The checkbox filter is applied as written instead of expanding parents.** Ticking a parent already ticks all its subcategories, so the filter already lists exactly what's checked. Expanding it was what added unchecked subcategories back. Other category filters, and other reports such as Spending and Cash Flow, still include a parent's subcategories.\n- **A subcategory checked without its parent gets its own row.** Showing it under a parent the user unchecked was misleading. Hiding it would have dropped data the user asked for.\n- **The click-through query isn't changed.** It still asks for the parent and all its subcategories, combined with the report's filter. Because the filter is now applied as written, unchecked subcategories drop out without changing every graph's click handler.\n\n## UML Diagram\n\n## Tech Debt\n\n**Introduced**\n- In custom reports, a single typed filter like `Category is Food` now covers Food only, not its subcategories. This matches what the checkboxes already showed, but it differs from other reports, where the same filter includes subcategories.\n- `useSelectedCategories` in `CustomReport.tsx` still has its own copy of the logic for reading the checkbox filter, separate from the new `getSelectedCategoryIds` helper. It wasn't merged because the two behave differently when the filter is too complex for the checkboxes.\n- The issue's request to see each subcategory on its own is only partly met. The Table view nests subcategory rows under their parent, but the graphs still show one bar per parent.\n\n**Encountered**\n- Dashboard widgets don't pass the report's filters to the graphs (`GetCardData.tsx`), so clicking a bar in a widget ignores the report's filters.\n- The checkbox list and the report filter bar share one condition, so a filter typed by hand and a checkbox selection can't be told apart.\n- The report spreadsheet tests mock the database query, so the query results ignore the filters. Tests have to supply already-filtered rows themselves.\n\n## Related issue(s)\n\nCloses #100\n\n## Testing\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [ ] Release notes added (see link above)\n- [ ] No obvious regressions in affected areas\n- [ ] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude 600	+// Narrows getSubcategoryIdsByParent to the subcategories that are reported
601	+// inside their parent's row. With a category filter, a subcategory only
602	+// rolls into its parent when both are selected; one selected without its
603	+// parent gets a row of its own instead of showing under a parent that was
604	+// left out. `selectedCategoryIds` is undefined when every category is
605	+// selected.
606	+export function getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent(
607	+  subcategoryIdsByParent: Map<string, string[]>,
608	+  selectedCategoryIds: Set<string> | undefined,
609	+): Map<string, string[]> {
610	+  if (!selectedCategoryIds) {
611	+    return subcategoryIdsByParent;
612	+  }
613	+  const rolledUp = new Map<string, string[]>();
614	+  for (const [parentId, subcategoryIds] of subcategoryIdsByParent) {
615	+    if (!selectedCategoryIds.has(parentId)) {
616	+      continue;
617	+    }
618	+    const selectedSubcategoryIds = subcategoryIds.filter(id =>
619	+      selectedCategoryIds.has(id),
620	+    );
621	+    if (selectedSubcategoryIds.length > 0) {
622	+      rolledUp.set(parentId, selectedSubcategoryIds);
623	+    }
624	+  }
625	+  return rolledUp;
626	+}

630	-// get undefined and match on their own id as usual.

640	+// Category filters the custom report's category selector can't show:
641	+// several category conditions, a category group condition, or a category
642	+// condition matching on names or tags.
643	+export function isComplexCategoryCondition(
644	+  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
645	+): boolean {
646	+  return (
647	+    conditions.some(
648	+      ({ field, op }) =>
649	+        field === 'category' &&
650	+        [
651	+          'contains',
652	+          'doesNotContain',
653	+          'matches',
654	+          'hasTags',
655	+          'hasAnyTag',
656	+        ].includes(op),
657	+    ) ||
658	+    conditions.filter(({ field }) => field === 'category').length >= 2 ||
659	+    conditions.some(({ field }) => field === 'category_group')
660	+  );
661	+}
662	+
663	+// The category condition the custom report's category selector shows as
664	+// checkboxes, if there is one.
665	+export function getSelectorCategoryCondition(
666	+  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
667	+): RuleConditionEntity | undefined {
668	+  if (isComplexCategoryCondition(conditions)) {
669	+    return undefined;
670	+  }
671	+  return conditions.find(
672	+    cond =>
673	+      cond.field === 'category' &&
674	+      ['is', 'isNot', 'oneOf', 'notOneOf'].includes(cond.op),
675	+  );
676	+}
677	+
678	+// The categories checked in the custom report's category selector, or
679	+// undefined when every category is.
680	+export function getSelectedCategoryIds(
681	+  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
682	+  categories: Pick<CategoryEntity, 'id'>[],

// its rolled-up subcategories hold, so it covers its own id and theirs.
// Other rows get undefined and match on their own id as usual.
export function getRolledUpCategoryIds(
  id: string | undefined,
  subcategoryIdsByParent: Map<string, string[]>,
): string[] | undefined {
  const subcategoryIds = id ? subcategoryIdsByParent.get(id) : undefined;
  return subcategoryIds && id ? [id, ...subcategoryIds] : undefined;
}

// Categories that are reported inside their parent's row rather than as a
// row of their own. Totals add up top-level rows only, so leaving these
// out is what keeps a subcategory from being counted twice.
export function getNestedSubcategoryIds(
  subcategoryIdsByParent: Map<string, string[]>,
): Set<string> {
  return new Set([...subcategoryIdsByParent.values()].flat());
}

// Subcategories of hidden parents, which the budget page hides along with
// their parent.
export function getSubcategoryIdsOfHiddenParents(
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): Set<string> {
  const hiddenParentIds = new Set(
    categoryGroups
      .flatMap(group => group.categories ?? [])
      .filter(cat => cat.hidden)
      .map(cat => cat.id),
  );
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  for (const [parentId, subcategoryIds] of getSubcategoryIdsByParent(
    categoryGroups,
  )) {
    if (hiddenParentIds.has(parentId)) {
      subcategoryIds.forEach(id => ids.add(id));
    }
  }
  return ids;
}

// Marks rows of a hidden parent's subcategories as hidden, so they're left
// out of reports the same way the parent is.
export function hideSubcategoriesOfHiddenParents(
  rows: QueryDataEntity[],
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): QueryDataEntity[] {
  const hiddenIds = getSubcategoryIdsOfHiddenParents(categoryGroups);
  if (hiddenIds.size === 0) {
    return rows;
  }
  return rows.map(row =>
    row.category && hiddenIds.has(row.category)
      ? { ...row, categoryHidden: true }
      : row,
  );
}

// A report filter on a parent category covers its subcategories too, the
// same way the parent's report row includes them: "is" and "one of" match
// the whole family, "is not" and "not one of" leave the whole family out.
// Filters on the category's name are left as they are.
export function expandSubcategoryConditions(
  conditions: RuleConditionEntity[],
  categoryGroups: Pick<CategoryGroupEntity, 'categories'>[],
): RuleConditionEntity[] {
  const subcategoryIdsByParent = getSubcategoryIdsByParent(categoryGroups);
  if (subcategoryIdsByParent.size === 0) {
    return conditions;
  }
  const withSubcategories = (ids: string[]) => [
    ...new Set(
      ids.flatMap(id => [id, ...(subcategoryIdsByParent.get(id) ?? [])]),
    ),
  ];

  return conditions.map(cond => {
    if (
      cond.field !== 'category' ||
      !['is', 'isNot', 'oneOf', 'notOneOf'].includes(cond.op)
    ) {
      return cond;
    }
    const ids = Array.isArray(cond.value) ? cond.value : [cond.value];
    if (!ids.some(id => subcategoryIdsByParent.has(id))) {
      return cond;
    }
    const excludes = cond.op === 'isNot' || cond.op === 'notOneOf';
    return {
      ...cond,
      op: excludes ? 'notOneOf' : 'oneOf',
      value: withSubcategories(ids),
    };
  });
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 13:32:19Z)**_

I've reviewed PR #128 by James Leonard: [[AI] Fix custom reports counting unchecked subcategories in their parent's total](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget/pull/128). It's a solid PR. The fix is correct and well tested, but two files that have nothing to do with the fix should come out before merging. All CI checks pass (test, typecheck, lint, VRT, e2e). I read the diff and the surrounding code but didn't run the app or the tests locally.

## What it does
Issue #100: in custom reports, unchecking a subcategory didn't change anything. Its money still counted in the parent's total. The reason was that `expandSubcategoryConditions` added every subcategory back whenever a parent was in the filter. The PR changes three things:
- **Filter applied as written:** a new `expandReportConditions` leaves the checkbox filter alone and still expands any other category filter to include subcategories.
- **Roll-up only when both are checked:** a new `getRolledUpSubcategoryIdsByParent` folds a subcategory into its parent's row only when both are checked. A subcategory checked without its parent gets its own row.
- **Shared helper:** the "too complex for the checkboxes" check moved out of `CustomReport.tsx` into a helper that the report code also uses.

The logic holds up. Clicking a bar still filters on the parent plus all its subcategories, and the report's filter (now left as written) is ANDed with that. So the transaction list matches the bar without touching any graph's click handler. The tests cover the cases that matter: an unchecked subcategory, a subcategory checked without its parent, Budgeted mode, and the click-through.

## Issues

**1. Should fix: two files unrelated to the fix**
- **`.github/workflows/temp-update-vrt.yml`:** the second commit, "Regenerate VRT snapshots", only adds this file. It doesn't change any snapshots. The workflow only runs on pushes to `fix/update-vrt-snapshots`, so it never ran on this branch. It's marked TEMPORARY, and it has `contents: write` and pushes commits automatically, which shouldn't end up on `master`.
- **`stryker.config.json`:** this is a config file from `stryker init` at the repo root, probably left over from a mutation-testing assignment. It has nothing to do with this fix.

**2. Team decision: typed filters now behave differently**
The PR admits this under Tech Debt, but it deserves an explicit OK from the team. A filter typed into the filter bar, like `Category is Food`, now matches only Food and not its subcategories. That's because the report can't tell a typed filter from a checkbox selection. Any saved custom report or dashboard widget that relies on such a filter will quietly show smaller totals after this merges. The Spending and Cash Flow reports still include subcategories for the same filter.

**3. Minor cleanups**
- [subcategories.ts `expandReportConditions`](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/subcategories.ts): when there is a checkbox filter, the `.map(...)` branch does nothing. A checkbox filter only exists when there's no other `category` or `category_group` condition, so expanding the remaining conditions changes nothing. It could just be `return conditions;`.
- [CustomReport.tsx:56](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/CustomReport.tsx#L56): importing `isComplexCategoryCondition as checkComplexCategoryCondition` only to avoid clashing with a local variable is awkward. Calling the helper inline, or renaming the local, would read better.
- `useSelectedCategories` still has its own copy of the logic for reading the checkboxes. The PR notes this, and it's fine as a follow-up.

**4. Process**
- **Commit messages:** neither starts with `[AI]`, which the repo rules require (the PR title does).
- **Empty sections:** the PR description's Testing and UML Diagram sections are blank. James should fill in at least Testing with how he checked it by hand, since he's the one who tested it.

Want me to post this as a review on the PR (starting with 🤖, per the repo rules)? I can also check out the branch and run the report tests locally.
